title: UConn Smothers Butler for Title No. 3
dek: Butler shot 12 for 64, the worst in title-game history, as UConn ground out a 53-41 win and a third national championship to end an 11-game postseason run.

setup.text: UConn's season began with modest expectations. A year earlier the Huskies had lost in the second round of the NIT, and they were picked to finish 10th in the Big East. They started 10-0, winning the Maui Invitational, then went 9-9 in the league and lost four of their last five regular-season games.

Then they stopped losing: five wins in five days to take the Big East tournament, four more in the West Region as a No. 3 seed against Bucknell, Cincinnati, San Diego State and Arizona, and a 56-55 national semifinal win over Kentucky. Kemba Walker, a consensus first-team All-American, came in averaging 23.7 points.

Butler, the No. 8 seed out of the Southeast, was in its second straight title game, the lowest-seeded finalist since Villanova in 1985. A year earlier Gordon Hayward's half-court heave had barely missed in a 61-59 loss to Duke; Hayward had since left for the NBA, and the Bulldogs had won 14 in a row.

Jim Calhoun, 68, was one win from joining John Wooden, Adolph Rupp, Mike Krzyzewski and Bob Knight as the only coaches with three national titles or more. UConn and Butler had never played each other.

story.text: The first half was a grind. Walker missed his first five shots. UConn led 13-8 after his three-point play with 12:34 left, then scored six points the rest of the half and went 0 for 5 from 3-point range. Shelvin Mack's 3 with a second left sent Butler to the locker room up 22-19.
Calhoun said his halftime adjustment came down to outwilling and outworking Butler. UConn kept pounding the ball inside and finished with a 26-2 edge in points in the paint.

Butler opened the second half 2 for 25 from the field. For more than 13 minutes it made one field goal, and a 25-19 lead became a 41-28 deficit. The Bulldogs missed their first 21 shots in the paint and made three two-point baskets all night.

Freshman Jeremy Lamb scored all 12 of his points after halftime. Alex Oriakhi had 11 points, 11 rebounds and four blocks, Roscoe Smith blocked four more, and Butler's stars, Matt Howard and Mack, combined to shoot 5 for 28.

sequence.text: Shelvin Mack hits a 3 with a second left in the half. Butler leads 22-19.
Chase Stigall rebounds his own miss and hits a 3 twenty seconds into the second half. Butler leads by six, its biggest lead of the night.
Jeremy Lamb buries a 3 off Tyler Olander's pass. UConn leads and never trails again.
Lamb picks off Mack and runs out for a dunk. Butler calls timeout.
Shawn Vanzant's jumper, from Stigall, is Butler's only field goal between 19:40 and 6:13.
Walker's twisting, scooping layup off Lamb's pass makes it an 11-point game. Butler calls another timeout.
Andrew Smith's putback is Butler's first basket in the paint all night, after 21 misses there.
Alex Oriakhi dunks Shabazz Napier's pass and makes the free throw. UConn leads by 14, its largest margin.
Walker makes two free throws, the game's last points.
Before the clock even runs out, Calhoun is pumping his fists and hugging an assistant while the Huskies head for the sideline and the confetti.

quotes.text: You see the tears on my face. I have so much joy in me, it's unreal. It's surreal. I'm so happy right now.
quotes.role: UConn guard, Final Four Most Outstanding Player

quotes.text: ...from a purist standpoint, if you really like defense, take a clip of this game.
Without question, 41 points and 12 of 64 is not good enough to win any game, let alone the national championship.
From last season and the loss to Virginia Tech, Coach, he gave me the keys. And from that point on, I just drove.

aftermath.text: Walker, who finished with 16 points and nine rebounds, was named the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player.
Counting three wins at the Maui Invitational, UConn went 14-0 in tournament games and finished 32-9.
Butler became the fourth team to lose back-to-back national championship games.
Calhoun still had a three-game suspension to serve at the start of the next Big East season, part of NCAA sanctions over recruiting violations.

legacy.text: Butler's 18.8 percent broke a title-game record that had stood since 1941, and its 41 points were 10 fewer than any finalist had scored in the shot-clock era.
At 68, Calhoun became the oldest coach to win the national championship and the fifth to win at least three. He said his father had taught him that you are known by the company you keep.
It was UConn's third national championship, after 1999 and 2004, won in the program's fourth trip to the Final Four.
